# Jacobson’s Local-Horizon Thermodynamics

Jacobson’s 1995 result is a conditional local theorem: if every local causal horizon carries one universal entropy per area and satisfies the equilibrium Clausius relation with matter boost energy at the Unruh temperature, then the metric obeys the Einstein equation up to a cosmological constant. The argument derives an equation of state from thermodynamic premises; it does not derive those premises or describe gravity as a force caused by an entropy gradient.

The primary source is [[vendor/entropic-gravity/sources/papers/gr-qc-9504004-jacobson-thermodynamics-spacetime.pdf|Jacobson 1995]]. This note uses \(c=k_B=1\) until constants are restored.

## Local equilibrium horizon

At an arbitrary spacetime point \(p\), choose a small spacelike two-surface element \(\mathcal P\). One side of the boundary of its past is generated by an orthogonal null congruence and serves as a local Rindler horizon \(\mathcal H\). Let \(k^a\) be an affinely parametrized generator with affine parameter \(\lambda=0\) at \(\mathcal P\).

Choose \(\mathcal P\) so that the expansion and shear vanish at \(p\):

$$
\theta|_p=0,
\qquad
\sigma_{ab}|_p=0.
$$

This is the local-equilibrium condition. Near the chosen generator, the approximate boost Killing field is

$$
\chi^a=-\kappa\lambda k^a,
$$

where \(\kappa\) is an arbitrary normalization of boost time.

## Heat flux and temperature

The boost energy of matter crossing the horizon is treated as heat:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta Q
&=\int_{\mathcal H}T_{ab}\chi^a\,d\Sigma^b \\
&=-\kappa\int_{\mathcal H}
\lambda T_{ab}k^ak^b\,d\lambda\,dA.
\end{aligned}
$$

The associated Unruh temperature is

$$
T=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi}.
$$

Assume a constant, universal entropy density \(\eta\) per horizon area:

$$
\delta S=\eta\,\delta A.
$$

Neither \(\eta\) nor its microscopic degrees of freedom are calculated in the argument.

## Area focusing

The null Raychaudhuri equation in four dimensions is

$$
\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda}
=-\frac12\theta^2
-\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}
-R_{ab}k^ak^b.
$$

Because expansion and shear vanish at \(p\), the leading term is

$$
\theta=-\lambda R_{ab}k^ak^b+O(\lambda^2).
$$

Consequently,

$$
\delta A
=-\int_{\mathcal H}
\lambda R_{ab}k^ak^b\,d\lambda\,dA.
$$

## From Clausius to Einstein

Demand the equilibrium Clausius relation

$$
\delta Q=T\,\delta S
$$

for every local horizon through every point and for every null direction. Matching the two integrands gives

$$
R_{ab}k^ak^b
=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar\eta}
T_{ab}k^ak^b
$$

for every null vector \(k^a\). Therefore there is a scalar field \(\Phi\) such that

$$
R_{ab}+\Phi g_{ab}
=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar\eta}T_{ab}.
$$

Assume local stress-energy conservation,

$$
\nabla^aT_{ab}=0.
$$

The contracted Bianchi identity then fixes \(\Phi\) up to a spacetime constant and yields

$$
G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}
=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar\eta}T_{ab}.
$$

Matching the standard normalization gives

$$
G=\frac{1}{4\hbar\eta}
$$

in \(c=k_B=1\) units. With entropy measured in ordinary units,

$$
\eta=\frac{k_Bc^3}{4G\hbar}.
$$

The cosmological constant appears as an integration constant and is not determined.

## Logical ledger

### Assumed

- smooth Lorentzian geometry and local equivalence-principle kinematics;
- an approximate boost symmetry and Unruh thermality of the local vacuum;
- universal, local horizon entropy density proportional to area;
- equilibrium at the chosen horizon element;
- matter stress flux as heat;
- the Clausius relation for all null directions; and
- local stress-energy conservation.

### Derived

- the null-null curvature relation;
- the full Einstein equation after Bianchi identity and stress conservation; and
- the relation between \(G\) and the assumed entropy-area coefficient.

### Not derived

- the horizon microstates or the area law;
- the numerical entropy density independently of measured \(G\);
- matter equations or stress conservation;
- the value of \(\Lambda\);
- quantum corrections or quantum gravity; or
- a literal force \(F=T\nabla S\) acting on a particle.

The result is strongest when read as a universality statement: very sparse local thermodynamic assumptions select the Einstein tensor as the consistent equation of state.
